markdown_report:
The next experiment should establish reliable GRU context encoding before testing whether removing older history helps.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Matched prefix removal reduced training margins across all four categories. This challenges indiscriminate cropping but does not estimate cropped-training effects. (2) Supplied padding discrepancies decreased from roughly 1.6–2.0 to 0.0010–0.0023. Numerical calibration must distinguish recurrence defects, readout errors and computation-path variation. (3) Strong sampled pairwise separation does not establish competition near the benchmark’s top-10 boundary.

**Insights from related work.** (1) GRU biases and recurrent terms remain active with zero inputs [1]; floating-point differences require separate controls [2]. (2) TimeSHAP measures recurrent sensitivity without establishing user motives [3]. (3) Sampled metrics differ from full-catalog metrics [4]. (4) CL4SRec, CoSeRec and recurrent augmentation precedents limit cropping’s novelty [5–7]. Their objectives and supervision differ from this experiment. (5) GRU4Rec’s negative pools and loss normalization can confound apparently matched targets [8].

The resulting directions are encoding correctness, controlled context intervention, and ranking-focused diagnosis:

| Layer | Existing evidence | Unresolved question | Proposed control |
|---|---|---|---|
| Encoding | Padding-dependent features | Semantic or numerical? | Masked recurrence and precision controls |
| Learning | Cropping loses matched margins | Context, supervision or regularization? | Matched candidates and connected gradients |
| Ranking | Positive sampled margins | Does top-10 membership improve? | Unchanged host HR@10 |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive and negative assessment.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Padding-calibrated matched cropping [1–3,5–8] | 4: interpretable combination; established components | 7: resolves confounds; gains unmeasured | 6: fixed backbone; exact controls demanding |
| Full-context recency-weighted loss [3,7] | 3: atomic intervention; familiar weighting | 6: preserves history; suppresses older targets | 2: simple weights; normalization matters |
| Training-prefix top-10 audit [4] | 3: targeted diagnosis; established ranks | 7: exposes competition; training optimism | 4: existing scorer; catalog cost |

**Selected idea: padding-calibrated matched cropping.** At 10% progress, retain this feasible, falsifiable experiment. Compare aligned states, final features and scores against unpadded and explicitly masked recurrent references. Predeclare absolute/relative tolerances, calibrate numerical variation, and investigate higher-precision discrepancies without retrospectively relaxing thresholds.

Then compare unchanged training A, full-context matched suffix supervision B, and cropped-context identical supervision C. Freeze half-history cropping, candidates, loss normalization, connected prefix gradients and full-context inference. C−B estimates the context-policy intervention; B−A estimates supervision allocation under fixed candidate construction. Neither proves stale-interest removal; deterministic-suffix training remains a later regularization control.

Predeclare an affordable common schedule and select one complete condition by four-category macro validation HR@10. Each trial trains one model/category; deploy one checkpoint/category. Preserve seeds, routing, diagnosis interfaces and predictor consistency. Report incomplete comparisons. Limit validation queries; audit popularity shortcuts and acknowledge training, candidate and selection uncertainty.

References: [1] [GRU](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html); [2] [numerics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html); [3] [TimeSHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00073); [4] [sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/); [5] [CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14395); [6] [CoSeRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.06479); [7] [Tan et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08117); [8] [GRU4Rec losses](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf).

idea.description: Test stochastic old-prefix removal after calibrating GRU padding invariance. Compare unchanged training A, full-context training with matched suffix supervision B, and cropped-context training with identical suffix supervision C as separate experimental conditions. Each trial trains exactly one independent GRU4Rec model per category. Select one complete condition using four-category macro validation HR@10 and deploy exactly one checkpoint per category without fusion.
idea.motivation: Supplied diagnostics show that removing old context lowers matched training margins, while residual padding discrepancies exceed the original absolute tolerance. These observations justify checking encoding and measurement semantics before interpreting context interventions. They neither establish harmful older history nor predict cropped-training validation performance. Qualitative feedback motivates recency hypotheses but does not establish ownership, compatibility requirements or latent intent. At 10% research progress, a controlled intervention remains preferable to adding learned selectors. Cropping has substantial precedent, so its contribution here is experimental identification rather than a new model class.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use the supplied corrected GRU4Rec rather than reconstructing unavailable implementation details. Inspect its actual loss, sampler and padding semantics during host implementation; do not assume that it uses the official GRU4Rec objective or session-parallel batching. No filesystem inspection or training is required in this writing call.

First diagnose existing padding behavior without changing it. Freeze one checkpoint, use eval() and no_grad(), disable autocast, and reset recurrent states for independent histories. Compare the same chronological real tokens under different left-padding lengths, batch companions, permutations and singleton evaluation. Compare aligned valid-token outputs, final features and identical candidate-score vectors separately. Record device, dtype, PyTorch/CUDA/cuDNN versions and precision settings. Repeat identical executions and batch-versus-singleton controls to characterize numerical variation. Investigate discrepancies with version-supported TF32 controls and FP64 where supported. Deterministic execution does not guarantee equality across computation paths.

Predeclare the elementwise criterion abs(actual-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference). FP32 atol=1e-5 and rtol=1.3e-6 can serve as an initial engineering threshold, not a universal GRU guarantee. Report maximum absolute error, maximum normalized tolerance violation, first divergent valid token, candidate-score errors, top-10 changes and boundary margins. Retain the original absolute-only diagnostic for continuity, separately from this richer criterion. Do not increase tolerances retrospectively to force a pass. A failed tolerance alone does not identify a semantic defect. If each candidate score changes by at most epsilon, a reference pairwise gap greater than 2*epsilon preserves its ordering; near-tie swaps alone provide weak evidence of padding leakage.

Use both an unpadded singleton reference and, for unresolved cases, an explicit recurrent reference built from the trained GRU weights. At every layer and padding position preserve the previous hidden state with where(valid, proposed_state, previous_state). Match PyTorch's reset/update/new gate order, biases and reset-after-hidden-projection candidate equation exactly. Include any baseline input/output transforms when comparing model features. Run this reference in evaluation mode so dropout does not confound comparisons. Agreement with the reference localizes discrepancies more effectively than packed-versus-singleton comparison alone.

If a semantic recurrence defect is confirmed, correct it uniformly before all conditions. Compact nonpadding inputs chronologically into internally right-padded sequences, pack nonempty rows, run the original unidirectional GRU, unpack, and scatter valid outputs to their original B x L positions. Never pack left-padded tensors directly. Preserve embeddings, dropout and recurrent layers; restore aligned B x L x H log2feats outputs. Read the greatest nonpadding index in the original layout, never count-1; return the baseline-compatible empty-history result explicitly. Verify no cross-example state leakage and finite nonzero gradients through retained embeddings and recurrent parameters. Update the embedded predictor writer and verify checkpoint-loaded predictor scores against training-model scores. If encoding remains unresolved, report the confound and withhold mechanistic context conclusions.

Predeclare A/B/C, common E<=200, exactly 200 batches per epoch, final-epoch checkpoint selection, a validation-query cap and charged time allocations within the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. A complete design requires twelve category-condition fits across separate trials; each trial trains only its selected condition's four category models, with one GPU and no internal ensemble. Choose E using available charged timing evidence; count failures, diagnostics and training against the shared budget. If a complete comparison is unaffordable, report it as incomplete rather than presenting an unmatched contrast. Preserve the baseline optimizer, dimensions, objective, clipping, schedule and sampling semantics. Do not treat four concurrent slots as four separate budgets.

For each row of n real inputs, retain all inputs unless a dedicated probability-0.5 branch draws K uniformly from max(1,ceil(n/2)) through n inclusive; keep the final K real inputs. Empty rows contribute no supervised loss; singleton rows remain unchanged. The inclusive upper bound makes actual removal probability lower than 0.5. Keep original aligned positive and negative targets at retained positions. Each supervised positive remains outside its causal input prefix, even if it appears later in the full teacher-forced sequence; the backbone must remain unidirectional. Do not reconnect targets across removed positions or pair arbitrary interior crops with the original final target. Use full permitted histories at inference.

A uses all baseline-valid positions. B uses full input with supervision restricted to retained positions. C removes the old prefix and uses exactly B's retained target positions. Keep full-context prefix states connected to suffix losses in B; detaching them introduces an additional gradient-horizon intervention. Freeze exact minibatch membership/order, candidate IDs and multiplicities, accidental-positive filtering, negative sampling probabilities and corrections, score activation, temperature, objective coefficients, optimizer steps and schedule. Construct the baseline candidate pools before applying the supervision mask and reuse them across conditions, including A where compatible, so masking targets does not silently remove in-batch negatives. The actual baseline construction takes precedence; document any unavoidable difference and narrow the interpretation of B-A accordingly. Identical seeds alone do not establish matching pools.

Preserve A's baseline reduction. For a positionwise objective already averaged over valid positions, use sum(mask*loss)/sum(mask) for B/C and apply the same retained-position treatment to positionwise score regularization. Do not average masked zeros over the original tensor. Keep global parameter regularization unchanged. If the actual objective has coupled batch normalization, first define its valid retained-loss decomposition rather than assuming independent position losses. Do not divide BPR-max or TOP1-max a second time by the negative count. For sampled cross-entropy, preserve the baseline sampling correction, if present, rather than inventing logQ correction. Report any reduction difference from A; B-A can otherwise include gradient-scale and regularization-balance changes. Use the same declared handling of empty supervised batches in B/C and log skipped updates.

Use separate deterministic crop randomness so crop draws cannot alter initialization, base sampling or negative pools. Match initialization, base samples and crop plans across B/C using explicit plans or keys containing category, epoch, batch and row. Keep crop RNG separate from model/dropout RNG. Preserve baseline dropout behavior; different shapes or execution paths can still produce different masks, so disclose residual stochastic differences rather than asserting identical trajectories. Equal targets and updates do not imply equal gradients, supervision budgets or runtime. Log valid/retained position counts, retained-length distributions, negative-pool summaries, actual optimizer steps and charged GPU-seconds.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Keep the pinned evaluator unchanged: 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negative candidates and evaluation seed 42. Select the complete condition with highest equal-weight macro validation HR@10; break exact ties A, then B, then C. Do not mix category winners, average checkpoints or combine scores. Each category loads exactly one independently trained model. Do not read other trials, reuse their checkpoints, access hidden tests, fetch extra data/pretrained weights or modify host evaluation.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and ModelView.model, item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data and review_data. Use the actual trained view.model; restore its previous mode after probes, including on failure. Accept (None, sequence, positive, negative) batches of B x L tensors. Return measured metrics and metric_definitions with counts and explicitly unavailable values. Context and margin diagnostics remain conditional training measurements, not validation HR@10. Use only histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; unavailable ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores, ownership and simulator traits must not be reported as observed. Preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five per category. Obtain timestamp strata only through a reliable history-to-probe alignment; otherwise mark them unavailable.

Supplementary training-prefix catalog audits must exclude the target from its input and define eligible competitors explicitly. Use fixed probes, candidate sets and training-derived popularity/history-length strata, report sample sizes, and distinguish performance on fitted training histories from held-out generalization. Audit whether gains concentrate on popular targets or short histories. Such audits may reveal shortcuts but cannot replace the fixed selection metric. Restrict adaptive validation queries and avoid tuning cropping probability or retained fraction in this experiment. Deterministic suffix training is a later optional control for stochastic regularization, not a prerequisite added silently to the twelve-fit design; arbitrary length-matched crops introduce target-gap confounds.

If host per-user validation hits are exposed, use 10,000 paired within-category user bootstrap replicates with an analysis-only seed-42 generator, shared resampling indices across conditions and equal category weights. Report category and macro C-B and B-A differences with percentile intervals and hit/miss transitions where available. If only aggregate HR is exposed, mark paired intervals unavailable. One changed hit corresponds to 0.5 percentage points of category HR and 0.125 percentage points of macro HR. Intervals condition on checkpoints and fixed candidates, excluding training-seed variability, candidate-resampling variability and adaptive selection bias; they are exploratory and not multiplicity-adjusted. No validation or test improvement has yet been established.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare A/B/C, p=0.5, minimum retained fraction=0.5,
common E<=200, 200 batches/epoch, final-checkpoint rule,
validation-query cap, tie order A then B then C, and charged budget.
Each separate trial trains one condition and one model per category.
Confirm that all twelve category-condition fits are affordable.

Encoding gate:
  freeze a supplied GRU4Rec checkpoint; enter eval/no_grad
  disable autocast; record precision settings and software/hardware versions
  for fixed training histories:
    reference = evaluate chronological real inputs without padding
    compare equivalent left-padded, batched and permuted versions
    measure aligned valid states, final features and identical candidate scores
    check abs(error) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference)
    report errors, tolerance violations, first divergence and ranking changes
  calibrate with repeated-run and batch/singleton controls
  investigate unresolved cases using precision controls and an explicit
  trained-weight GRU reference that skips padded state updates at every layer
  if a semantic defect is confirmed:
    correct recurrence/readout uniformly in model and predictor writer
  if unresolved:
    report confounding; do not attribute effects to historical context

For each separately executed condition in [A, B, C]:
  for category in required_four_categories:
    initialize supplied corrected GRU4Rec with seed 42
    reset dedicated base-sampling, negative-pool and crop streams
    for epoch in range(E):
      for batch_index in range(200):
        _, x, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch(...)
        candidates = baseline_candidate_pool_before_supervision_mask(...)
        # Explicitly identical pools, multiplicities and filtering across B/C.
        valid = baseline_valid_supervision_mask(x, positive, negative)
        keep = false_mask_like(x)
        for each nonempty row:
          positions = chronological_nonpadding_positions(x[row])
          n = len(positions)
          K = n
          if dedicated_crop_rng.uniform() < 0.5:
            K = randint_inclusive(max(1, ceil(n/2)), n)
          keep[row, positions[-K:]] = True
        context = x with positions outside keep zeroed if condition == C else x
        supervised = valid if condition == A else (valid & keep)
        reset independent-example recurrent states
        features = padding_safe_GRU_log2feats(context)
        # In B, preserve gradient paths through earlier full-context states.
        loss = actual_baseline_objective_with_fixed_candidates(
            features, positive, candidates,
            supervised, documented_identical_B_C_reduction)
        # Positionwise losses: sum(supervised*loss)/sum(supervised).
        # Match positionwise score regularization; retain global regularization.
        # Preserve max-loss normalization and baseline sampling corrections.
        update_one_model_using_baseline_schedule(loss)
        log retained counts, actual updates and charged time
    save final checkpoint and matching predictor artifacts
    run charged interface, recurrence and predictor-agreement checks
  obtain unchanged host four-category macro validation HR@10

Report complete-condition C-B and B-A, category differences,
supervision counts, stochastic limitations and charged time.
If exposed, bootstrap paired validation-user hits within categories;
otherwise report aggregate scores without invented intervals.
Select one complete condition by macro HR@10; ties prefer A, then B, then C.
Deploy its one checkpoint per category with full-context inference.
Never fuse scores, checkpoint parameters or independently fitted components.

padding_safe_GRU_log2feats(x):
  allocate zero aligned outputs [B,L,H]
  compact each nonempty row's real inputs chronologically
  right-pad internally; pack with CPU lengths and enforce_sorted=False
  run the original unidirectional GRU; unpack and scatter to original positions
  return aligned outputs, including explicit empty-row behavior

final_readout(x, features):
  index = maximum position where x != 0
  gather features at index for nonempty rows
  apply declared baseline-compatible behavior for empty rows
  never use count_nonzero-1 in the original left-padded coordinates

originality.positive: Combines numerical calibration, matched candidate construction and connected-gradient controls to make a familiar augmentation experiment more interpretable.
originality.negative: Padding-safe recurrence, sequence cropping, recurrent input corruption and controlled ablations have established precedents; this is primarily an experimental design contribution.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish encoding artifacts, supervision changes and context-policy effects before investing in learned history selection or recency weighting.
future_potential.negative: Validation gains remain unmeasured; the experiment does not isolate stochastic regularization or establish stale-interest mechanisms, and one-seed sampled evaluation limits generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains the GRU backbone and baseline objective, with input and supervision masks providing clear integration points.
code_difficulty.negative: Explicit recurrent references, numerical calibration, exact candidate matching, loss-specific normalization, RNG control, budgeted comparisons and embedded predictor consistency require substantial care.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Defines recurrent equations showing that zero-valued inputs do not guarantee unchanged hidden states.
Documents packed-sequence interfaces and the gate equations needed for a trained-weight recurrent reference.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied implementation contains a padding defect.
Provides no evidence that prefix cropping improves recommendation accuracy.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy guidance
contributions: Explains why mathematically equivalent batched and sliced operations can produce different floating-point results.
Supports separating semantic encoding errors from numerical discrepancies.
limitations: Does not supply a universal acceptable tolerance for this GRU.
Numerical agreement alone does not validate the recommendation objective.

related_work.title: TimeSHAP: Explaining Recurrent Models through Sequence Perturbations
contributions: Provides attribution methods for recurrent sequence models.
Motivates examining event contributions through controlled sequence perturbations.
limitations: Attribution does not establish users' causal motives.
Inference-time perturbations do not estimate retraining effects from cropped contexts.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes limitations of sampled ranking metrics as estimates of full-catalog performance.
Motivates distinguishing the pinned benchmark objective from supplementary catalog audits.
limitations: Does not justify changing the required host evaluator.
Does not predict which GRU intervention improves the fixed sampled benchmark.

related_work.title: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation (CL4SRec)
contributions: Uses sequence augmentations, including contiguous cropping, to construct contrastive views alongside next-item prediction.
Provides precedent for treating cropping as augmentation rather than evidence of stale-interest removal.
limitations: Crops need not retain the latest interaction and have different supervision semantics from aligned suffix-target training.
Its Transformer results do not establish GRU-specific recency benefits.

related_work.title: Contrastive Self-supervised Sequential Recommendation with Robust Augmentation (CoSeRec)
contributions: Adds correlation-aware substitution and insertion to sequential contrastive augmentation.
Restricts destructive augmentation for short histories, motivating explicit retained-length reporting.
limitations: Does not directly evaluate the proposed matched-supervision GRU intervention.
Its augmentation and contrastive-learning effects cannot be transferred as evidence of suffix-cropping gains.

related_work.title: Improved Recurrent Neural Networks for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Uses prefix/next-item expansion and stochastic input embedding dropout in recurrent recommendation.
Distinguishes input regularization from temporal adaptation through recent-session fine-tuning.
limitations: Prefix expansion changes the supervised-instance budget.
Embedding dropout and temporal fine-tuning are different interventions from matched suffix cropping.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces ranking objectives including BPR-max and TOP1-max with softmax-weighted negative contributions.
Explains why negative construction and loss normalization are material experimental controls.
limitations: The supplied corrected baseline may use a different objective or sampler.
Official session-based implementation details must not be assumed to describe the host's user-history training.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides concrete implementations of candidate sampling and GRU4Rec losses.
Illustrates how batch targets and additional frequency-based samples can affect negative pools.
limitations: Does not replace inspection of the supplied baseline during implementation.
Matching positive targets alone does not reproduce its candidate multiplicities, filtering or normalization.

related_work.title: PyTorch CUDA semantics and precision controls
contributions: Documents CUDA precision controls relevant to diagnostic comparisons.
Supports recording execution settings and disabling reduced-precision paths when investigating discrepancies.
limitations: Supported controls vary with software version and hardware.
Disabling TF32 or enabling determinism does not guarantee equality across different kernels.

related_work.title: PyTorch testing and comparison semantics
contributions: Defines absolute-plus-relative numerical comparison semantics.
Provides dtype-dependent default tolerances useful as initial engineering references.
limitations: Default tolerances are not universal guarantees for recurrent computations.
Passing a feature comparison does not establish ranking quality or generalization.
